items.title: Live: Israel launches strikes on Lebanon's capital as residents flee
items.description: The US president says the son of assassinated supreme leader Ali Khamanei would be "unacceptable" to him, as an evacuation order in Lebanon sparks panic.

items.title: Understand what's happening in Iran today in 381 words from Laura Tingle
items.description: The ABC's global affairs editor, Laura Tingle, is in Dubai and is providing daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: A 'party' in emergency was how some Iranians found out about the war
items.description: Many Iranians feel like they are on the cusp of freedom after the US and Israel launched strikes on Saturday. But some also distrust the motives of both countries and are calling for an immediate end to the war.

items.title: Israel threatens to ‘bring hell’ to Beirut as war rapidly widens
items.description: The US–Israeli campaign against Iran continues to expand, with Israeli evacuation orders across the southern suburbs of Beirut raising fears in the rapidly widening war.

items.title: Live: Minister insists RAAF planes sent to Middle East will focus on repatriations
items.description: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke has insisted that the Australian military aircraft sent to the Middle East will be focused on repatriating Australians. Follow live.

items.title: Wildcards that could crash Australian superannuation
items.description: A major market meltdown would change the financial plans of millions of Australians overnight. With the Middle East war, how likely is it?

items.title: 'He lies': Subject of spiked ABC Australian Story episode a convicted child sex offender
items.description: A "plucky pensioner" from a cancelled Australian Story episode is a convicted child sex offender who has failed to pay his victim more than $385,000 in civil damages.

items.title: Live: Oil spikes 4pc while Australian dollar tumbles 1pc, ASX to fall
items.description: A tumble on Wall Street is likely to send Australian stocks sharply lower, while oil prices surged 4 per cent as the Middle East war enters its sixth day. Follow the latest updates in our live blog.

items.title: The hole in Mark Carney's speech
items.description: When Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney addressed federal parliament on Thursday, his well-crafted speech had one gaping hole.

items.title: NSW Health apologises to whistleblowing doctors over misconduct probe
items.description: NSW Health apologises to three senior doctors at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital after a two-year confidential investigation was found by the NSW Ombudsman to be unreasonable and unfair, in the latest example of dysfunction within two key departments.

items.title: Donald Trump fires Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem
items.description: Kristi Noem has been under pressure over her handling of immigration enforcement operations.

items.title: Bucking, ethics and OnlyFans: What is the future of Australian rodeo?
items.description: Australian rodeos are caught in a high-stakes hustle to keep the outback alive in a country that some argue is outgrowing the buck.

items.title: Muslims 'should not be forced to beg' for protection, Labor MP says
items.description: Labor backbencher Ed Husic says Islamophobia should be examined as part of Royal Commission into Antisemitism and Social Cohesion.

items.title: Gold Coast mayor says ratepayers did not fund Trump estate visit
items.description: ABC News can reveal more details about the Gold Coast mayor's visit to Mar-a-Lago before a Trump Tower deal was inked.

items.title: The Matildas embody Aussie pub rock spirit against Iran, and they're playing to win
items.description: The Joe Montemurro incarnation of the Matildas feels like a throwback to classic Australian rock. And in their Asian Cup win over Iran, they showed their mantra of playing free, but always going for the win, is starting to pay off.

items.title: Man wins seatbelt fine court battle as AI traffic cameras face scrutiny
items.description: A Queensland court decision casts fresh doubt on the reliability of controversial AI road-safety cameras after clearing a driver fined when his passenger moved their seatbelt during a trip.

items.title: How a popular beauty routine may put workers at risk
items.description: Walk-in nail salons are a mainstay of shopping hubs across Australia, but not enough is known about the health problems nail technicians face. Experts say it is time that changed.

items.title: 'Reference Man' is why your office air conditioning is so cold
items.description: Phones, cars, and the temperature in an office were all designed to suit the average man. Researchers say women are an afterthought in the way many products and spaces are designed.

items.title: 'It's killing people softly with grooves': How Cold Chisel changed their sound
items.description: Jimmy Barnes may be a rockstar with powerhouse vocals, but he's also a music history expert who loves gardening and cooking with his wife.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: A shock radio departure, a promising study and a Canadian visit
items.description: It's been a big week in the news. Did you catch these stories?

items.title: Pygmy possum with long fingers rediscovered in remote rainforest
items.description: A possum and a glider long thought extinct have been rediscovered in New Guinea by a group including Australian mammalogist Tim Flannery.

items.title: Aussies name flag-bearers for Winter Paralympics opening ceremony
items.description: Ben Tudhope and Georgia Gunew will be Australia's flag-bearers at the opening ceremony for the Milano Cortina Games.

items.title: India survives Bethell onslaught to book T20 World Cup final spot
items.description: India has survived a brilliant century from England's Jacob Bethell to record a seven-run win in a thrilling men's T20 World Cup semifinal at Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium.

items.title: New e-bike and e-scooter bans 'excessive', retailers say
items.description: As the government considers the recommendations, one retailer says the focus should be on banning high-powered electric bikes rather than a blanket ban on young riders.

items.title: Aston Martin drivers 'risk permanent nerve damage' driving for too long
items.description: Aston Martin will almost certainly not finish this weekend's Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix, if it even starts at all, over fears the vibration of the car could permanently injure its drivers.
